title: Palestrina knot
subtitle: A knotted line stitch with a series of raised knots along a foundation thread
excerpt: Palestrina knot builds a decorative line with a series of raised knots at regular intervals. Each knot is tied around the previous stitch, giving a beaded or corded line. It is also called the tied coral stitch and is used for heavy textural outlines.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Palestrina stitch entry. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), knotted outline stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776).

glossaryTerms.definition: The locking action in Palestrina knot where the thread is passed through a loop formed around the previous stitch, tying a firm raised knot at each stitch interval.

heroPrompt: Palestrina knot line in dark burgundy perle cotton on cream linen, showing the evenly spaced raised knots along the line, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Palestrina knot creates its beaded line through a
at each stitch interval. A small stitch is taken into the fabric at each knot point, the thread forms a loop, the needle passes through the loop to lock the knot, then the line continues.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Perle 8 or stranded cotton 3 strands for clear knot definition

content.text: Bring the thread up at the start of the line. Take a small stitch into the fabric at the first knot position.
Without pulling through completely, pass the needle under the small stitch from top to bottom.
Pass the needle through the resulting loop (going left to right) and pull gently to form the knot.
Move along the line to the next knot position and repeat. Keep knot spacing even throughout.

items.symptom: The knots are not raised or visible
items.cause: Pulling the knot thread too tight, collapsing the knot flat.
items.fix: Allow each knot to tighten gently until it sits on the surface. Stop pulling before the knot disappears into the fabric.

items.cause: No guidance marks on the transfer line.
items.fix: Mark evenly spaced dots along the transfer line before starting. Each knot position is one dot.

content.text: Palestrina knot produces a bold decorative line used in Italian embroidery and crewelwork. The knotted tie principle appears in other tied line stitches including coral stitch and snail trail stitch.
